results.summary_before: This is a hardware implementation of the Simon Says memory game. The game uses four buttons and four LEDs to display a growing sequence of colors, each with a corresponding tone played on a speaker. It also supports a two-digit 7-segment display for showing the score. The design requires an external 50 kHz clock and is documented with wiring instructions, including a Wokwi online simulation for reference.

results.summary_before: This project implements a finite state machine in Verilog that detects the overlapping bit sequence '1001' and indicates detection by displaying '8.' on a 7-segment LED display, otherwise showing '-'. The design includes a test mode where holding the condition inputs high allows individual segment testing or digit display by varying the bidirectional pins. It needs an external 7-segment LED display wired to the eight outputs and a switch or signal source to drive the serial input. The documentation is clear about operation and testing, though it is a straightforward educational FSM exercise.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit single-cycle microprocessor with a register file and ALU, designed to execute a simple instruction set supporting basic ALU operations, load/store, and carry status checks. It is controlled through input pins for register addresses, opcode, and data, with outputs providing register data or processor status. The design was tested with twelve testbenches covering ALU operations, data movement, and load/store, though timing interactions between instructions were not exhaustively verified. It lacks a program counter and external memory, so jump operations are omitted, and it operates entirely in simulation without external hardware.

results.summary_before: This is a 3-bit ALU that computes addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulo in parallel, with a 3-bit selector choosing which result appears on the 6-bit output. Inputs A and B are set with switches, and the selector uses three more switches to pick one of the five operations, with the result shown on six LEDs. The documentation explains the selector encoding and provides examples, and the design is purely combinational. It is an educational project requiring external switches and LEDs for input and output.

results.summary_before: The design is a CDMA modulator and demodulator that uses two 5-bit LFSRs to generate Gold codes and spreads a 1-bit input signal. It is tested via a Verilog testbench and intended for lab experiments with an oscilloscope, where an external op-amp simulates channel noise to measure bit-error rate. The circuit recovers the original signal through a receptor output and indicates a valid seed via an LED. The project was created as part of a Latinpractice Bootcamp to study CDMA and Gold sequences.

results.summary_before: This is a two-axis position controller that uses 4-bit counters, comparators, and a state machine to move X and Y positions towards user-set targets. The user sets 4-bit target values on the input pins and triggers motion with a button; the current positions are output as 4-bit values for each axis. External hardware includes switches for inputs, a push-button for motion, and LEDs or a logic analyzer for outputs. The design operates at up to 50 MHz and can be reset asynchronously.
